answer: River-Sampled Prism Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function assigns identities to small task groups; the assignment is unknowable until the epoch seed is revealed and only resolves after registration closes. An attacker flooding identities must commit real work per identity (a distinct key plus bandwidth) before learning which groups they land in. A jetty rule: any group whose membership exceeds a random size threshold is voided, forcing re-entry and doubling attacker overhead per surviving identity.
